page: Amazon Web Services r7i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a custom 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 physical cores and 64 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 512.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual processor. The instance does not bundle dedicated GPUs or local ephemeral storage, directing all input-output operations through network-attached block storage. Baseline network capacity is rated at 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results show robust memory throughput and compute execution. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 216.54 GB/sec on large blocks, paired with write bandwidth of 95.05 GB/sec. Geekbench evaluation registers a single-core score of 2118.0 and a multi-core score of 19182.0, with PassMark CPU overall scoring reaching 72798.2. In real-world data processing workloads, the instance achieves 76.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 75.35 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 extensions assists vector math and CPU-based inference, posting 36.38 tokens per second on text generation using 7B parameter models.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory allocation delivers high memory density per core, making it resource-efficient for setups where memory capacity is the limiting constraint rather than raw execution throughput. The absence of local disk requires external volume attachments, which introduces dependence on network storage performance for persistent file storage. The configuration fits large in-memory caches like Redis, memory-intensive relational databases, distributed stream processing, and enterprise application servers requiring large working sets.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.16xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by custom 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processors running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is configured with 32 physical cores presenting 64 dedicated vCPUs, 105 MB of L3 cache, and 512 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. It features 25 Gbps baseline network throughput and includes advanced instruction sets such as Intel AMX and AVX-512 for accelerated compute tasks. The instance does not include local ephemeral disks or dedicated GPUs, requiring network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmarks record strong uncached memory read bandwidth of 216.54 GB/sec and over 76 million Redis SET operations per second. The r7i.16xlarge provides high memory density relative to core count, making it an efficient solution for Redis clusters, high-concurrency database backends, large in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing workloads.
